title: How to unearth young stars, the Bayern Munich way
description: Bayern Munich initially aim to find local young players from Bavaria before looking further afield - here's how they do it.
article_context:
Bayern initially aim to find young players from Bavaria before looking further afield
Bayern Munich are one of the elite powers in European football and current home of Ballon d'Or winner and England captain Harry Kane.
But, while Kane is the latest hugely successful foreign import at Bayern, the German giants also put a particular focus on producing their own elite young talent.
In 2013, Bayern had four homegrown players in the starting line-up as they won the Champions League.
Repeating that victory, and continuing the club's history of nurturing young players, is what director of youth development and campus Jochen Sauer says Bayern are aiming for.
Sauer joined from RB Salzburg in 2017 when the academy campus opened in another part of Munich, away from the first-team training complex.
The club's motto "Mia San Mia" translates to "we are who we are" and Sauer says it has always been the club's goal to have a local homegrown element in its senior side.
"It was always our identity and philosophy to be a regional club, but at the same time to be competitive internationally and on Champions League level," Sauer tells BBC Sport. "But always having a core of our team coming from the Munich area and the Bavarian region with a deep identification with the club and the city.
"Our recruitment guidelines, especially for the under-11 to the under-15 teams, is trying to recruit as much talent as possible from the Munich area and the region of Bavaria."
Munich-born Croatia international Josip Stanisic is a good example. The midfielder, 26, signed as an under-17 player from local outfit SC Furstenfeldbruck, while 22-year-old Aleksandar Pavlovic joined the academy aged eight and has worked his way up to the first team and is a Germany international.
But perhaps the biggest name to come out of the academy in recent times is Jamal Musiala. The former Chelsea youth player, who joined aged 16, is a star for Bayern and Germany and has already won six Bundesliga titles at just 23 years old.
It was part of the club's strategy to bring in the best young foreign players, and those with German passports, to the club, but they also enjoyed a bit of luck.
The move came around the time Bayern Munich were interested in then-Chelsea winger Callum Hudson-Odoi, who shared the same agent as Musiala, who moved from Germany to England when he was seven.
Bayern were already aware of Musiala because he was born in Germany, but the timing was right to make a deal happen.
"There were for sure some pieces that came together at that time," Sauer says.
"I think one reason why we fought for the player at that time was the reason we had the feeling that Chelsea is not really seeing his full potential to be a top player for their first team.
"Because, otherwise, if they would have seen him as a future prospect, then it would been hard, even for Bayern Munich, to get a player out of the Chelsea environment."
Other young players in the first-team squad include 18-year-old Bara Sapoko Ndiaye, signed from Gambinos Stars Africa in The Gambia, and 18-year-old Lennart Karl, who joined the academy four years ago and has been capped by Germany.
Shirts with Bayern's academy graduates adorn the walls of their youth campus
The Bayern Campus can house up to 43 players in accommodation, predominantly local players before they widen the search overseas.
"I think there is basically kind of a guideline that we want to have a minimum 60% of the players coming from the region and reaching the level of the under-19 age group," Sauer says.
"This automatically means that the other 40% of the team has to be recruited from other regions nationwide.
"Coming to an age group of under-17, we are also reaching out to the main European football markets to recruit the most talented players internationally.
"Jamal Musiala is one perfect example. As soon as we're coming to an age of 16 and the regulations allow us to do international transfers, we want to recruit the best talents in Europe. That's for sure part of our recruitment philosophy."
Another piece that fell into place for Musiala was the Bayern under-17 team at that time was coached by Miroslav Klose, the former Bayern forward who is the record goalscorer for Germany.
Klose is credited with pushing Musiala to work on the defensive side of his game. He also knew what a player needed to get to the highest level, with the former striker becoming an assistant to Hansi Flick when Musiala joined the first team.
That idea of having former players in charge of the next generation continues.
Ex-Bayern centre back Dante, who also played for Nice for more than 10 years, is the current under-19 head coach.
"They can inject a little bit of the Bayern Munich DNA into the players," Sauer explains. "More from a personality side, not necessarily from a playing style.
"He also has some different ideas on the playing style but you know playing for Bayern Munich and being in the first team of Bayern Munich, at least they can tell our players what they have to be from a character, from a personality to make it up to the first team."
With so many players coming into the system and a difficult first-team set-up to break into, the Bayern style remains consistent throughout age groups.
Coaches are given guidelines to work towards but it does not stop them from having their own ideas as they aim for a style of "dominance and intensity".
"But football is always a process of evaluation," Sauer says.
"Opening the campus in 2017, we have put a very clear idea of football in place, but always kept the openness to add in ideas from coaches like [Jupp] Heynckes, [Julian] Nagelsmann, [Thomas] Tuchel, Hansi Flick, and, for sure, [current Bayern manager Vincent] Kompany. The football is always developing.
"So we have to be open enough always to amend little things. But I would say that the overall strategy is still what it was in the times of Heynckes, Pep Guardiola or Louis van Gaal."
There is an eye-catching display in one of the well-kept corridors of Bayern's campus. Shirts of high-profile academy graduates are framed on the walls, with a display showing tiers of Germany's football leagues and players who have played in them.
To qualify for the display, players need to have played a minimum of 30 full 90-minute games.
Bayern say that almost 44% of the young players who are in their youth set-up until the under-19 team become a professional player.

title: Haaland admits 'you start questioning everything' when Man City fail to win
description: Erling Haaland has reacted to Manchester City's latest failure to win by "questioning everything."
article_context:
Erling Haaland has reacted to Manchester City 's latest failure to win by "questioning everything."
City required an 86th-minute equaliser from Rayan Cherki to draw 2-2 against Napoli on Tuesday at the Etihad in the Champions League.
Napoli had twice taken the lead, and City's failure to take three points means they have won just one of their past seven matches in all competitions.
"We tried to push at the end for a goal but we couldn't," Haaland told TNT Sports. "Not good enough and we let them in too easily.
"We were not able to control and attack the game in the way we want.
"Football is easy and difficult. When you win it's easy and you know what to do. When you don't you start questioning everything.
"The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy.
"We have so much quality so it's about getting the quality out in every payer.
"We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best."
Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund gave Napoli a 55th-minute lead, before teasing the home support about his allegiance to the red half of the city.
Ayyoub Bouaddi equalised before Noa Lang gave Napoli the lead again. But Cherki rescued a late point which leaves City sixth in the league phase of the Champions League after five matches.
"I don't care about my goal, I wanted to win the game," Cherki told TNT Sports.

"We tried to put all we have inside the pitch. Sometimes the game is not like you want, and today is like the last game, the last two or three games. We need to work more and come back for a win, just that."
City manager Enzo Maresca said: "We pressed very aggressive, we recovered the ball most of the time. Off the ball I think the team was good, from my point of view.
"We created a lot of chances but it was difficult. We expected Napoli to play a waiting game in a low block.
"We conceded few chances, and the goals we conceded could have been avoided.
"There is a degree of regret we didn't win but when you can't win, don't lose. We take the point and go forward."
Press Association contributed to this report.
headline: Haaland cuestiona todo tras empate 2-2 de City contra Napoli
caption: Erling Haaland admitió que el empate 2-2 ante el Napoli en la Champions League lo lleva a cuestionar cada detalle del juego. El equipo inglés necesitó el gol de Rayan Cherki en el minuto 86 para evitar la derrota, tras haber concedido dos ventajas al rival y acumular solo una victoria en sus últimos siete compromisos. La reacción del delantero subraya la presión sobre un Manchester City que busca recuperar su nivel. ¿Podrá el conjunto volver a la regularidad que lo caracterizaba?

title: Rinderknech denies refusing doping test
description: French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test.
article_context:
Arthur Rinderknech is yet to win an ATP title and reached a highest world ranking of 24th in May
French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test.
L'Equipe reported on Wednesday , external that the current world number 57 is under investigation by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA).
It relates to a "surprise" test in June, with French newspaper L'Equipe claiming there was a "possible misunderstanding with the sample collector".
Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova is currently serving a four-year ban for refusing to take an out-of-competition doping test in December 2025, and has appealed against the decision.
Rinderknech issued a statement on Instagram in response to L'Equipe's report, saying: "I have already advised the ITIA that I deny the allegation and I have already requested that the matter be heard and determined by an independent tribunal, as is my right."
The 31-year-old, who beat current world number one Alexander Zverev in the first round at Wimbledon last year, believes he will then be "exonerated of the test refusal allegation".
"I have never taken any banned substance and I am proud of my accomplishments in professional tennis, all of which have been achieved through hard work and with integrity always," he added.

title: 'Two faces' & rudely named set-pieces end Hibs' long wait for home win
description: Hibs show they are capable of winning ugly with the help of a beautiful goal as Marink Reedijk guides them to a first home league win in nearly eight months against Dundee.
article_context:
Marink Reedijk ended Hibernian's long wait for a home league win
Hibernian got an enormous monkey off their back in the battling 2-1 win over Dundee at Easter Road on Tuesday night, finally ending their home hoodoo.
Martin Boyle put them in front from the penalty spot before a glorious Nicky Cadden curler made it two before half-time and those goals proved enough for a first league win in Leith since 4 April.
That is 243 days, or seven-and-a-half months. However you slice it, it's too long for a club of Hibs' stature.
Head coach Marink Reedijk broke that sorry sequence at the fourth time of asking, having lost his previous home games against Falkirk, Celtic and Dundee United.
Before the League Cup semi-final against rivals Hearts at the start of this month, there was talk of the Dutchman being under early pressure.
Instead he secured Hibs' first win over their bitter rivals at Hampden and has now won three of his past four matches.
Are we getting a clearer picture of Reedijk's team and is a corner being turned?
Before the win over a similarly-dejected Dundee, following their 8-0 hammering by Hearts, Reedijk rejected talk of a home jinx.
The notion was a valid one. Hibs had lost nine of their previous 10 home league games, including a 4-0 drubbing by Dundee United at the weekend.
However, the former Beveren manager does not seem prone to superstition or intangibles. He is a straight talker and hammered home the need to nail the "brilliant basics".
Hibs hardly blew Dundee away in front of a sparse Easter Road crowd, but dominated possession and had more accurate passes and balls into the final third than their opponents.
The win was the most important thing and they had to scrap for the three points after Joe Wright hauled Dundee back into the game in the second half.
"It's also capable to show two faces - a nice way of playing football, but also that we can be a team with the knife between the teeth, survive in a match and get over the line," said Reedijk, who is building a reputation for a neat turn of phrase.
On Saturday, Hibs were second to most balls, struggled to show any identity and looked lost tactically.
"I think it's a good reaction to what we did against Dundee United," Reedijk added.
"I saw a front foot team again, I saw togetherness again, I saw a team who fought for every ball.
"That's not easy, they have to be patient, you have to be secure, you have to wait for your moment and we took these moments and that was really good to see.
"As long as we keep ourselves, I think these are good signs."
'An absolute peach!' - watch superb Cadden strike
Cadden's stunning strike came from a smartly-engineered corner routine, with the left-back having gone close from a similar situation earlier in the match.
Reedijk singled out assistant coach Rogier Molhoek for devising the set-piece plans, joking that the codes used are rather rude.
He added: "It was a beautiful goal, wasn't it? It was one when it left the foot, I was like, 'ooh, he hits it well and you saw the angle of the ball'. Then, when I didn't see the keeper getting close to the ball, I was like, 'oh, this is in'.
"We try to use every quality we have in order to make it difficult for opponents to see what we are doing in the beginning. Also we look at their organisation and if their organisation allows us to attack certain spaces, we try to do this.
"This is the job of Rogier, he always makes routines. He will always give a little touch, a little twist, in order to surprise – and also with crazy names. You will never know these names because sometimes it's not polite."

title: Why Man City can't wear their new kit in Premier League
description: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why Manchester City will not be able to wear their new fourth kit in the Premier League.
article_context:
Manchester City will only be wearing their orange kit for selected Champions League games
Manchester City sported a new orange fourth kit during their Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday - but will not be able to wear it in the Premier League.
Top-flight clubs in England can only wear a maximum of three strips in a league campaign, meaning Enzo Maresca's side cannot play in their new kit.
However, there is no limit in the Champions League, meaning City can wear their new strip for the rest of their European campaign.
City can also wear the kit in the FA Cup, provided that an application is made to the Football Association, as well as a reason for its requested use.
That is why Arsenal were allowed to play in a white fourth strip in the 2025-26 FA Cup as part of their campaign to combat youth knife crime in London.
Fans could scan the badge on City's 2025-26 fourth kit to receive items in a video game
City also released a green fourth kit in 2025-26 with a gaming-inspired theme.
The kit, debuted during their Champions League victory over Villarreal, featured an NFC chip in the club badge that fans could scan to unlock gaming rewards.
The club released another fourth kit in the 2024-25 season co-designed by Noel Gallagher in tribute to the 30th anniversary of Oasis' 1994 album 'Definitely Maybe'.
It was worn in the Champions League by the men's team against Inter Milan and Paris St-Germain, and the women's team against Paris FC and Barcelona.
A fifth kit was also used by the men's team during the 2025 Club World Cup
During the 2023-24 season, the women's side also sported a Chinese New Year-inspired shirt in a League Cup victory against rivals Manchester United .
While the Premier League is more restrictive over the number of kits that can be released - the rules are more relaxed in other European leagues.
Napoli wore 13 strips during the 2021-22 season; including a Halloween kit, four different Diego Maradona tributes and four Europa League-specific kits.

caption: US Soccer debe elegir al sucesor de Mauricio Pochettino con criterio técnico, no como figura mediática. El resumen sugiere que, aunque contar con Pep Guardiola sería ideal, lo esencial es un entrenador que afine al equipo y mejore su rendimiento. La presión por un nombre de renombre no debe eclipsar la necesidad de experiencia táctica. ¿Podrá la federación encontrar un técnico competente que realmente eleve al conjunto nacional?

title: El premio Monumental que se merecen los hinchas de River para terminar el año con una alegría
description: Como sugirió Ponzio y suscribe Otamendi, los hinchas se merecen el título: jugando bien o mal, la gente llenó el Liberti en un semestre lleno de golpes duros.
article_context:
Los hinchas de River, siempre fieles al equipo (REUTERS/Agustin Marcarian).
"Esta hinchada se merece ser campeón” . No es ninguna casualidad que Leonardo Ponzio haya compartido en las últimas horas una historia en su cuenta de Instagram con un vlog de los fanas de River cantando este clásico hit. Porque la gente realmente cumplió con creces con el aliento para el equipo del León en el Monumental en este segundo semestre de 2026 repleto de frustraciones y con el título del Clausura como la única alegría posible de la temporada, que además cuenta con la yapa de la clasificación a la Copa Libertadores 2027.
Los hinchas no juegan, es cierto, no pisan el césped de la cancha. Pero está claro que los 85.000 fanáticos de River que colmaron las tribunas del Liberti en cada partido del equipo como local en la segunda mitad del año cumplieron una función vital para el sostén anímico y la motivación de los futbolistas . Brindaron un apoyo incondicional, que tiene un valor superior en los momentos malos. Por eso, Ponzio destacó tras la victoria frente a Lanús en los octavos del Clausura que “la gente tiene un párrafo aparte por cómo nos aguantó”, explicó que “el hincha es la historia de este club”. Y el capitán Nicolás Otamendi se comprometió -y comprometió al grupo- en “dejar la vida por ustedes (los hinchas) y por estos colores” porque entiende que “estamos en deuda”.
El mata-mata contra Lanús fue otra muestra del amor de la gente por la camiseta. Y lo que contagia en el equipo cuando hace vibrar los cimientos del renovado Monumental.
Un total de 843.000 personas en los diez partidos que River jugó en Núñez después del Mundial, y nada menos que con la eliminación de la Copa Sudamericana de por medio. Solamente frente a Estudiantes de Río Cuarto , en el fin de semana largo que incluyó el feriado del lunes 12 de octubre, las tribunas del Liberti no estuvieron del todo completas: hubo 78.000 espectadores , una cantidad que sin dudas hubiese explotado cualquier otra cancha del fútbol argentino.
Y esto no fue, porque la gente estuvo de visitante y de local . Claro, el equipo de Ponzio sintió el aliento en las canchas de Banfield (con 7.000 personas en el debut del León como DT), Belgrano (10.000), Atlético Tucumán (5.300), Sarmiento (4.500) y Aldosivi (10.000), el mismo rival que en los 16avos de la Copa Argentina: River metió 15.000 fanas en el estadio Padre Martearena de Salta.
Lógico que hubo murmullos en el Monumental . Reproches y expresiones en cantos de bronca e impotencia por el bajo rendimiento del equipo y varios errores individuales. Sin embargo, el domingo desde las tribunas bajaron únicamente gritos de aliento que levantaron a los futbolistas tras el empate de Lanús y les dieron impulso para ir en busca del triunfo en el comienzo del segundo tiempo.
Este escenario tiene un valor aún más preciado porque es posible que haya sido el último partido de River en su casa este año , ya que en cuartos de final visitará a Instituto en Córdoba y, en caso de llegar a las semifinales, solo volverá a jugar en el Monumental si enfrenta a Independiente: si avanza Vélez se jugará en Liniers porque el Fortín terminó 3° en la Zona A, mientras que el Millonario fue cuarto de la Zona B. Y la final, claro, será el sábado 12 de diciembre en cancha neutral, más precisamente en el Estadio Único de La Plata.
Como lo expresaron Ponzio y Otamendi, esta hinchada de River se merece ser campeón . Un premio Monumental por el plus que le aporta al equipo del León.

headline: River y su hinchada merecen premio Monumental tras victoria sobre Lanús
caption: Los 85.000 hinchas que llenaron el Monumental en la segunda mitad de 2026 fueron el motor del triunfo de River sobre Lanús en los octavos del Clausura. Leonardo Ponzio y Nicolás Otamendi destacaron que el aliento de la afición merece un reconocimiento especial, calificándolo como un “premio Monumental”. Con la clasificación a la Libertadores 2027 y la posibilidad de que sea el último partido en casa este año, la pregunta queda en el aire: ¿el apoyo masivo será suficiente para que River levante el título?

title: 'Most frustrating of career' - Martin on Foxes draw at Blackpool
description: Leicester City boss Russell Martin describes Tuesday's 1-1 draw with Blackpool as the most frustrating result of his career.
article_context:
A squandered victory at the seaside has redefined Russell Martin's definition of frustration.
The Leicester City manager said he was "hurt" by the solitary point his side picked up in Tuesday's 1-1 draw at lowly Blackpool in League One after dominating just about every facet of the game – controlling 77% possession and amassing 30 shots, of which nine were on target.
Asked if the draw was the most frustrating moment of the season, former Rangers and Southampton boss Martin replied by saying: "This season? Of my short but feels like very long managerial career."
That says a lot coming from a manager who was smuggled out of the stadium under police escort then sacked at Rangers after a draw with Falkirk last season, and whose Southampton side was once undone in the Premier League by two second-half Mohamed Salah goals after leading 2-1.
Those were tenure-defining defeats for a manager whose reputation has taken a battering in recent seasons, with his style of possession-heavy, passing football – an approach he once said was to "dominate the ball and be aggressive with it" , external – coming in for particular ridicule when results have gone against his side.
It has been the same at one-time Premier League title winners Leicester this season in the third tier, with Martin's method called into question in the early months of his tenure after the Foxes got off to a slow start.
Results have improved in recent weeks - they are unbeaten in six matches across all competitions and are up to seventh in the table.
But victory would have had them within a point of the play-off places, and Martin said the result will leave him "eternally frustrated".
"We should win, I know that, you know that and I think everyone in the stadium knows that. But we don't," he told BBC Radio Leicester after the match at Bloomfield Road.
"How we only score one goal, I'm really struggling to come to terms with.
"We have brilliant chances in the middle of their goal, not like half chances. And we actually score a goal that is really brilliant, but we shouldn't need a goal like that to win the game.
"I'm not frustrated, I'm hurt that we don't win the game and we concede a rubbish goal."
Is Leicester boss Martin turning the Foxes' fortunes?
Listen to BBC Radio Leicester's When You're Smiling podcast
It took more than an hour for the Foxes to break Blackpool's resistance, with a deluge of chances missed before Will Alves cut in from the left to beat home goalkeeper Bailey Peacock-Farrell with a shot that took a slight deflection.
It was six minutes from the end when Niall Ennis scrambled home the leveller for the Seasiders.
"I'm really proud of the players and how much they have grown in terms of what the performances look like," said Martin.
"But it's my job to be demanding of them, and there is no way we should be drawing that game. No way."

title: Transfer rumors, news: Man United's Bruno Fernandes wanted by Juventus
description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes, who is out of contract at the end of the season, is a target for Juventus. Transfer Talk has the latest.
article_context:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes ,who is out of contract at the end of the season, is a target for Juventus , while United and Barcelona want to sign United States winger Mathis Albert from Borussia Dortmund . Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.
Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades
- Juventus have expressed an interest in signing Manchester United attacking midfielder Bruno Fernandes as a free agent in the summer, according to Tuttosport . They will face competition from AC Milan , who will try to reunite the 32-year-old with coach Ruben Amorim.It is felt as though the summer isn't the time for Fernandes to move to MLS or Saudi Arabia . Fernandes addressed his future on Tuesday by saying : "For us to start winning games and then we can start speaking about a contract." Inter Milan 's Hakan Çalhanoglu is another midfielder being looked at by the Bianconeri .
- Manchester United and Barcelona have stepped up their interest in Borussia Dortmund and USMNT winger Mathis Albert , TEAMtalk reports. The race to sign the 17-year-old is already gaining momentum, and he is keen to play more regularly than he currently is under Niko Kovac, having got just 38 minutes in the Bundesliga so far this season. Albert has previously turned down approaches from Manchester City , Barcelona and Bayern Munich , while Chelsea , Paris Saint-Germain , Arsenal and Liverpool have also monitored him.
- Bayern Munich are considering moves for Liverpool pair Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz plus Manchester City winger Jérémy Doku as question marks hang over the futures of Michael Olise and Jamal Musiala , according to TEAMtalk . The Bavarians' long-running efforts to sign Ngumoha could be blocked as the Reds are close to finalising a new contract for the winger, their interest in Wirtz has never wavered and Doku's lack of Premier League starts could aid Bayern's chances. Olise is in the sights of Barcelona and Real Madrid while, according to Football Insider , Liverpool and Arsenal are long-term admirers of Musiala.
- AFC Bournemouth don't want to let Junior Kroupi leave in January and are demanding £100 million for the forward, according to talkSPORT . The 20-year-old is the subject of interest from Arsenal, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, with the latter also looking at Manchester United's Marcus Rashford . Even so, the Cherries are determined to keep their France international until the summer at least, and Kroupi would favour a move to Paris Saint-Germain whenever he leaves the Vitality Stadium.
- The relationship between AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and Roc Nation chairman Jay-Z could help bring Real Madrid forward Endrick to San Siro, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports. Brazil international Endrick, who is represented by Roc Nation, has started just one match for Madrid so far this season as the 20-year-old is firmly behind Kylian Mbappé in the pecking order. The 20-year-old enjoyed a successful loan spell at Lyon in the second half of last season, a move which Milan -- owned by media and sports investor Cardinale -- could look to replicate this term.
- AC Milan's search for somebody who can play left-back has seen them look at Manchester United's Noussair Mazraoui , Barcelona's Alejandro Balde , Frosinone's Gabriele Calvani and Bologna's Juan Miranda . ( Calciomercato )
- Napoli are seriously considering Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee regardless of whether or not Lorenzo Lucca departs. ( Sky Sports Italia )
- Juventus are looking at Atalanta's Gianluca Scamacca , Atlético Madrid's Alexander Sørloth and Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta after Luciano Spalletti asked for a tall and physically imposing striker. ( La Gazzetta dello Sport )
- Leeds United are in talks to extend Dominic Calvert-Lewin 's contract amid interest from Manchester United. ( Daily Mail )
- Brighton & Hove Albion are pushing to try to beat Real Madrid, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan to the signing of Atlético Mineiro centre-back Vitão . ( TEAMtalk )
- Brighton, Bournemouth, Brentford, Nottingham Forest, Newcastle United, Aston Villa, Sunderland, Fulham and Everton are all looking at Cruzeiro centre-back Jonathan Jesus . ( TEAMtalk )
- Roma are keen to sign Nottingham Forest winger Callum Hudson-Odoi on loan in January. ( Football Insider )
- Newcastle United are tracking Ajax centre-back Dies Janse , who also has interest from three other Premier League clubs. ( TEAMtalk )
- Atalanta sporting director Cristiano Giuntoli watched Eddy Kouadio during Monza's 3-0 win against Fiorentina. ( Nicolo Schira )
- Bologna sporting director Marco Di Vaio was also at the match to watch Leonardo Colombo and Ebenezer Akinsanmiro . ( Nicolo Schira )

title: Who are Sabah? Barça's Champions League opponents from near Iranian border
description: Sabah, a club near the Iranian border that didn't exist a decade ago, with a coach who owes his career to a Lithuanian quiz show, are in this season Champions League. How did they make it?
article_context:
As ever, the league phase of this season's UEFA Champions League is packed full of the biggest clubs on the planet.
From two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain to last season's beaten finalists Arsenal , from record 15-time winners Real Madrid to their bitter LaLiga rivals Barcelona , the competition showcases the best of the best from across the continent.
But among the great and the good of European soccer are some less familiar names, and some that was completely new to almost all fans around the world when the draw for this season's league phase was made. Sabah FK, making their debut in the competition this season, fall into that category. The team from Azerbaijan drew European giants Arsenal, Barcelona, and Manchester United for their first voyage at this level.
- Why Champions League's iconic 'star' match ball could soon be replaced - How world record for longest men's domestic unbeaten streak was broken
So, who are Sabah FK? How did they get the chance to go toe-to-toe with the biggest clubs in Europe. And what was their coach's unique route to European football's showpiece event? Here is what you need to know about them.
Editor's note: This article was first published on Aug. 27, 2026 and has been updated
Sabah FK was founded only on Sept. 8, 2017, so the club's first match in the Champions League proper may well fall on its ninth birthday. The team nicknamed The Owls hail from Masazir, around 20 miles north-west of Azerbaijan's capital Baku, with the Iranian border less than 200 miles south down the coast of the Caspian Sea.
Last season was a monumental one, not just for Sabah FK but for Azerbaijani football as a whole. Sabah won their first Azerbaijan Premier League title, completing a double by lifting the Azerbaijan Cup, and in the process breaking Qarabağ's grip at the top.
Baku-based Qarabağ had won 11 of the previous 12 league titles and last season became the first Azerbaijani club to reach the group or league phase of the Champions League, eventually losing to Newcastle United in the knockout phase playoffs.
Watch your favorite events in the newly enhanced ESPN App. Learn more about what plan is right for you. Sign Up Now
It has been a rapid rise for Sabah, but it all started in somewhat bizarre fashion.
They entered the league system in 2017-18 in the second tier, the Azerbaijan First League, and were promoted after one season despite the fact they finished fifth. The top four in the league -- Khazar Baku, Qaradağ Lökbatan, Shuvalan and MOIK Baku -- all failed to get the license needed to enter the top flight. Instead, the spot was given to Sabah, who never looked back.
The speed of Sabah's rise, plus tricky and expensive travel routes from Azerbaijan, has resulted in a modest away following at times for European games. When Sabah arrived in Romania to play the first leg of their Champions League playoff against Israeli clubs Hapoel Be'er Sheva (held at a neutral venue for security reasons), they were greeted at the team hotel by one solitary ultra.
That hardy fan, who had ventured alone from Baku to Bucharest to greet his heroes and put on a one-man firework show complete with pink flares for the surprised players, was later able to celebrate a 5-2 victory for his team that won the tie 6-4 on aggregate and secure the club's place in the Champions League league phase.
🇦🇿✈️🇷🇴 One Sabah FK fan showed up at the team hotel in Romania for their Champions League playoff, and the players were completely caught off guard. As the squad walked out, they stopped, smiled, and applauded him for the unreal gesture. Sabah FK are still a young club without... pic.twitter.com/YiJl0cWFsc
The tactical mastermind for Sabah is Valdas Dambrauskas, the first Lithuanian to lead a club into the Champions League league phase.
The 49-year-old's route to the top has been far from conventional. Dambrauskas never played football beyond the third tier in his homeland and retired at the age of 23, before he embarked on a coaching career. His life changed in 2002 when he appeared on "Šeši nuliai - milijonas," the Lithuanian version of "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire." Dambrauskas won 4,000 litas -- around $1,300 -- which he used to move to London where he earned his coaching badges while working various jobs, including delivering newspapers and childminding.
It was in England that Dambrauskas started his managerial career with Kingsbury London Tigers FC in the Spartan South Midlands Football League Premier Division -- the ninth tier. He led the club to its highest finish, the first step of a career that saw him land a domestic quadruple with FK Žalgiris in his homeland, win the Bulgarian league with Ludogorets and lift domestic cups in Latvia with RFS and Croatia with Hajduk Split before joining Sabah in 2025.
Sabah are the first team with pink as one of their main home kit colors to reach the group stage of the Champions League. Although they have opted to stick with a largely black shirt with pink accents for four consecutive seasons, the club's distinctive badge is equally pink and black, and the team's nickname is Qara-çəhrayılar (Pink-Blacks.)
The Azerbaijani champions used to play in blue and white before changing their colors in 2023-24. Pink is important to Sabah's hometown as its famous Lake Masazir is known for its distinctive pink coloring.
At no stage in Sabah's run to the league phase were they favorites to progress.
Sabah were unseeded in each of their matches against Welsh champions The New Saints, Finland's KuPS, AGF Aarhus from Denmark and Hapoel Beer-Sheva of Israel.
The crucial playoff round win over Hapoel Beer-Sheva was a real nail-biter. Sabah needed a 94th-minute goal in the second leg to keep their European dream alive and take the tie to extra time, eventually adding two extra-time goals to secure their spot.
Very few teams have managed to get through four games to reach the group or league stage of the Champions League. Only Kazakhstan's Kairat (2025-26), Slovan Bratislava of Slovakia (2024-25), Moldovan side Sheriff (2021-22), Sweden's Malmö (2021-22), Ferencvaros of Hungary (2020-21) and Serbian club Red Star Belgrade (2018-19 and 2019-20) have managed such an arduous path to the big time before Sabah.
headline: Sabah FK debutará en fase de grupos de la Champions
caption: El club azerbaiyano Sabah FK, fundado en 2017, llega a la fase de grupos de la UEFA Champions League tras ganar la liga y la copa locales y superar en la ronda de clasificación al Hapoel Be’er Sheva con goles en tiempo extra. Su entrenador, Valdas Dambrauskas, alcanzó la élite europea después de triunfos en Lituania, Bulgaria, Letonia y Croacia, y una curiosa aparición en un programa de preguntas. El ascenso meteórico del equipo, que juega en la zona de Masazir, plantea la incógnita de si podrá competir contra gigantes como Arsenal o Barcelona sin experiencia previa en la competición. ¿Logrará Sabah mantenerse en la élite europea o será una visita fugaz?

title: Which USMNT players could follow Pochettino to Manchester United?
description: Man United are a mess, but could Mauricio Pochettino turn to any of his former USMNT players to help pull the Red Devils out of the relegation zone?
article_context:
Mauricio Pochettino has traded in his blue United States tracksuit for a black Manchester United one, at least until his first big game at Old Trafford, when he will certainly break out a sharp, all-black suit.
In some ways, the task for Pochettino will be the same as it has been for every manager who has taken charge of the Red Devils since Sir Alex Ferguson walked away in 2013: returning one of the world's biggest clubs to the top of the sport. It's a task that's harder in an era when more and more rivals have the money they do -- if not, in the case of a few teams, even more -- and their own football operations department lags far behind. In other ways, what lies ahead for Pochettino is even more difficult than the quandaries that felled those who came before him because he takes over a Man United side that finds itself in the relegation zone, while still trying to balance UEFA Champions League football.
Pochettino has plenty of experience -- including stints at Espanyol , Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur , Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea -- to draw upon as he tries to solve the 13-year-old Manchester United problem, but what will he take from his time managing the USMNT to Old Trafford?
Maybe the question should be who he will take.
The U.S. might not have talent that Spain , Argentina or England do, but it does have players playing in the Premier League , across Europe and an expanding crop of exciting youngsters Pochettino started to integrate into the national team after the FIFA World Cup .
Might Pochettino grab a couple of Americans he became familiar with to help turn around Manchester United? If so, which players would make for smart signings and join Tim Howard and Jonathan Spector as modern Americans at Old Trafford?
Pochettino asks a lot of his fullbacks, which isn't great for a Manchester United side that counted those positions as weaknesses even under the less-demanding Michael Carrick. That's especially true on the left side, where Luke Shaw is still a useful player, but all action, up-and-down the pitch dynamism is not his forte even on the increasingly rare occasions he is fit.
The Fulham man is plenty proven in the Premier League, so he can be expected to step in and produce immediately. He's able to get way up the pitch and provide another wide attacking option, while still retreating into his spot in the back four and credibly defend. There is no other player in the world who has both done the job in the Premier League and for Pochettino before. He is uniquely qualified and, in other circumstances, would be Man United's first call Jan. 1.
Dan Thomas is joined by Craig Burley, Shaka Hislop and others to bring you the latest highlights and debate the biggest storylines. Stream on ESPN+ (U.S. only).
The problem? He is 29 years old and vital to the Cottagers as they, too, try to avoid the drop. It's hard to imagine Fulham sanctioning his departure on the cheap and no matter how much of a natural fit he'd be at Old Trafford, you'd have to think that the Red Devils' executives would balk at spending a tidy sum on someone of his age. His contract is up in 2028, though, so maybe the price is a little more reasonable than you'd otherwise think.
If Robinson is the older, most proven option to solve a fullback question, then Freeman is the fast-rising upside bet.
The son of a Super Bowl winner is a tremendous athlete, but his development on the ball and reading the game have seen him become one of the most intriguing young defenders in the world over the past couple of years. In 2024, he was playing for Orlando City SC 's reserve team; by 2025, he was an MLS Best XI selection and in 2026, he shined at the World Cup before becoming a regular for Villarreal.
Pochettino put a lot of trust in Freeman, calling him up and immediately throwing him into the Gold Cup . Even as the youngster was sorting out some of the finer points of the sport, Pochettino ran him out time and time again, giving him 13 caps in 2025 and another 15 in 2026.
Whether it was as a fullback, as a wingback or even tucking into the outside of a back three, Freeman won Pochettino's trust. In his debut World Cup, at just 21 years old, he rewarded Pochettino's faith with a series of fabulous performances on the biggest stage.
Freeman has been a favorite of Iñigo Pérez's at Villarreal too.
"We need them to be very versatile, and in this case, Alex is a super player," Pérez said last month . "He can easily play center back, fullback, left back, further forward, wingback; he's even played on both flanks for his national team. Therefore, this versatility and dynamism, combined with his skill level, means that, for a coach, the confidence to field him in any position or ask him to do things that might surprise him makes me bolder, and, as you've seen, he's able to play with astonishing composure."
Jumping to United might take a bit of an adjustment period for Freeman, but he has shown that he can develop at an astonishing pace. Betting on his talent, versatility and the existing trust Pochettino has in him could make him a United regular for the next decade.
Balgoun could be playing in the north of England right now, but a bizarre transfer deadline day saw the striker's move to Everton scuppered, and he has spent the past three months playing sparingly for Monaco before an expected January move out of the principality.
Could that pave the way for him to head to Old Trafford? The Red Devils need help up front, where Benjamin Sesko 's inability to kick on has left them too often pushing Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha out of position to the center forward spot.
Without tons of money available to spend, United probably cannot get the surefire, top-notch striker they'd ideally like, but Balogun has proven himself as a capable center forward at every level. He's not going to win the Golden Boot, but his well-rounded game is a good fit for Pochettino's system, as he proved at the World Cup, and he's the type of reliable front man the Red Devils desperately need so Mbeumo, Cunha and the rest of the attackers can get into their preferred positions and make the whole attack function.
Monaco are not in a position to demand a king's ransom for Balogun, who already showed he'd like a Premier League move. This is the type of good, stabilizing signing Manchester United need to make to shore up a problem spot.
Manchester United will be focused on adding players who can get them out of this tailspin and start laying a foundatio
headline: Pochettino podría apuntar a Alex Freeman para el United
caption: Según reportes, el nuevo técnico del Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino, tendría en la mira al lateral estadounidense Alex Freeman, quien ganó la confianza del entrenador en la Copa Oro y brilló en la Copa del Mundo con la selección. Freeman, versátil en varias posiciones defensivas y con experiencia reciente en Villarreal, podría ser la solución al problema de laterales que atraviesa United mientras lucha por salir de la zona de descenso y mantener su plaza en la Champions League. ¿Será la versatilidad de Freeman suficiente para revertir la crisis del United?

title: Wales and West Ham's Morgan suffers serious injury
description: Wales and West Ham winger Ffion Morgan faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering a serious knee injury.
article_context:
Ffion Morgan joined West Ham from Bristol City in 2025
Wales and West Ham winger Ffion Morgan is facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.
Morgan has undergone surgery having been helped off during West Ham's Women's Super League win over Charlton earlier this month.
The 26-year-old is now likely to miss the rest of the season.
"Ffion will now begin her rehabilitation programme under the supervision of the club's medical team," a West Ham statement said.
The injury also makes Morgan a major doubt for next summer's Women's World Cup, should Wales qualify.
Rhian Wilkinson's side take on Norway in a two-legged play-off final next week as they bid to reach the tournament for the first time in the nation's history.
Morgan, who has 56 caps, is an international regular and would be a shoo-in for the Wales squad if fit.
Five return for Wales' World Cup play-off final
Home World Cup can inspire Wales' future stars
She joined West Ham on a two-year deal in 2025 after her contract at Bristol City expired.
Morgan has also played for Cardiff City, Coventry United and Crystal Palace.
She suffered an ACL injury while playing for Wales Under-19s as a teenager, while she had only recently returned to action for West Ham after another lengthy fitness lay-off.
Wales face Norway at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later.
Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway may not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer.
The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway.

title: Why are there 2:05pm kick-offs in the Premier League on Sunday?
description: Our Ask Me Anything team explain why the Premier League fixtures have some unusual kick-off times this weekend.
article_context:
Everton's derby with Liverpool has been moved from Saturday to Sunday
The Premier League kick-off times look a little unusual this weekend, with no Saturday 12:30 GMT slot, and games starting at 12:00 and 14:05 on Sunday.
Everton will host local rivals Liverpool on Sunday at 12 noon because the match has been selected for live broadcast by TNT, who have a mid-day broadcast slot on that day. The game was originally scheduled for Saturday.
This has had a knock-on effect on the remaining fixtures.
On a typical Premier League weekend, the first matches will begin at 14:00 followed by a final 16:30 kick-off.
Pushing start times back five minutes to 14:05 reduces the risk of overlap with the unusual early 12:00 start time, while avoiding clashing with the 16:30 fixture.
Midweek European games have also affected the schedule, as the Premier League aims to prevent clubs from playing two matches within 60 hours of each other.
Crystal Palace , Sunderland , Bournemouth and Brighton are all set to play in the Europa and Conference Leagues on Thursday, ruling them out of Saturday Premier League fixtures.

title: Goalkeeper trains alone amid a 12-game ban after death of Spanish player
description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono is training on his own at the club's facilities, with no date set for his return to the team.
article_context:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono is training on his own at the club's facilities, with no date set for his return to the team.
Owono, who is serving a 12-match suspension for the challenge that led to the death of Tenerife forward Jesús De Miguel, has been having individual workout sessions at the club's headquarters since last week.
Owono made his first public appearance since the fatal collision on Friday when he attended Andorra's home league game against Leganés, where a minute's silence was observed for De Miguel prior to kick off.
De Miguel, 30, died on Nov. 3 after he suffered a cardiac arrest following an on-field collision with Owono during a Spanish second division game.
Following De Miguel's death, Owono, 25, requested to be left out of Equatorial Guinea 's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers this month.
- Gerard Piqué criticizes 12-match ban for Jesús Owono after Jesús de Miguel death - Erling Haaland: When Man City don't win 'you start questioning everything'
Andorra have not announced when Owono will return to training with the rest of his teammates.
Andorra owner Gerard Piqué recently admitted that Jesús " will need more than 12 matches before he is ready and able to compete."
But Piqué also criticized the length of the suspension: "My take on all this is that the 12-match ban imposed on Jesús Owono effectively blames him for consequences for which he was not at fault. I believe a sanction should be based on the action itself, not on the consequences.
Piqué's verdict was criticized by Tenerife coach Álvaro Cervera, who said : "In my immediate circle, outside of football, there are people who see these events differently... But I think he [Piqué] should look at the action itself. I haven't spoken out publicly, nor do I intend to, but I think it could have been avoided; I don't think it's the sort of thing we see every day, as he seems to suggest."
Andorra coach Carles Manso previously said that the decision about when -- and if -- to return would be Owono's.
"He is deeply affected by the situation," Manso said. "We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return. He can make that decision whenever he feels the time is right and he truly feels prepared to do so."
Owono called the aftermath of the incident "the most difficult days of my life" and added: "I struggle to find the words, and it is very hard for me to process anything that has happened.
"I feel an immense amount of pain over the loss of Jesús. My thoughts are with him, his family, and everyone who loved him.
"I know there will be many issues to address. I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. Right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything other than Jesús and the pain we are all experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesús."

title: Argentina vs. Dinamarca, hoy EN VIVO por el Mundial Sub 17: posibles formaciones, horario y por dónde ver
description: El equipo de Diego Placente buscará una victoria que le permita sellar la clasificación a la siguiente instancia. Seguilo en Olé.
article_context:
La Selección Argentina viene de ganarle a Mozambique en el Mundial Sub 17.
La Selección Argentina Sub 17 se jugará la clasificación a los 16avos de final del Mundial de Qatar 2026 cuando enfrente a Dinamarca , por la tercera y última fecha del Grupo C . El equipo dirigido por Diego Placente depende de sí mismo para avanzar de ronda y buscará cerrar la fase de grupos con una victoria que le permita meterse entre los 32 mejores del certamen.
La Albiceleste llega a este compromiso con tres puntos, producto de una derrota por 2-0 ante Australia en el debut y un triunfo por 2-1 frente a Mozambique en la segunda jornada , con goles de Matheo Machuca y Simón Escobar. Por su parte, Dinamarca acumula apenas una unidad: perdió 4-0 contra Mozambique e igualó 0-0 ante Australia. Argentina necesita ganar para asegurarse la clasificación y, dependiendo del resultado de Australia-Mozambique, podría quedarse con el primer puesto de la zona . Un empate la obligaría a estar pendiente de otros resultados y una derrota complicaría seriamente sus chances.
El partido entre Argentina y Dinamarca, por el Mundial Sub 17, se disputará este miércoles 25 de noviembre, desde las 12.30 (hora argentina), en el complejo Aspire Zone de Al Rayyan, Qatar . El encuentro se podrá ver en vivo por DSports y TyC Sports. Además, se podrá seguir el minuto a minuto con todas las incidencias a través de Olé.
La Selección Argentina se juega la clasificación a los 16vos de final del Mundial Sub 17 . Tras debutar con derrota ante Australia (2-0), el equipo de Diego Placente se recuperó y en la segunda fecha derrotó 2-1 a Mozambique para conseguir sus primeros tres puntos. Ahora, deberá derrotar a Dinamarca en la última fecha de la fase de grupos para conseguir la clasificación a los 16vos de final .
La Albiceleste depende de sí misma para meterse en los playoffs: con una victoria avanzará a la próxima ronda de la Copa del Mundo de Qatar. Caso contrario, deberá ponerse a hacer cuentas, sea para clasificar como segundo de grupo o para avanzar como uno de los mejores terceros. En Olé, te contamos todos los detalles de este partido.

title: A qué hora juega hoy Boca vs. Independiente Rivadavia y por dónde se puede ver EN VIVO el Torneo Clausura
description: El Xeneize vuelve a jugar en la Bombonera después de ganar la Copa Sudamericana y buscará dar otro paso en el campeonato ante la Lepra mendocina. Seguilo en Olé.
article_context:
Leandro Paredes en la final de la Copa Sudamericana (Foto: Fernando de la Orden).
Este miércoles, Boca recibirá a Independiente Rivadavia , por los octavos de final del Torneo Clausura 2026 . El encuentro se disputará en La Bombonera , donde el Xeneize volverá a presentarse ante su gente después de consagrarse campeón de la Copa Sudamericana en Colombia. El equipo de Rodolfo Arruabarrena buscará aprovechar el envión de la conquista internacional para seguir avanzando en el campeonato local y acercarse a una nueva final.
El Xeneize llega en un gran momento futbolístico: viene de vencer 2-0 a Atlético Mineiro en la final de la Sudamericana y también se quedó con el primer puesto de la Tabla Anual . En el Clausura terminó segundo en la Zona A, por lo que tendrá la ventaja de jugar como local en esta instancia. Sin embargo, el poco tiempo de recuperación después de la consagración podría llevar al entrenador a realizar algunas modificaciones. Por su parte, Independiente Rivadavia finalizó séptimo en la Zona B, con 23 puntos, y viene de perder la final de la Supercopa Argentina ante Estudiantes de La Plata . La Lepra mendocina intentará dar el golpe en la Bombonera y meterse entre los ocho mejores del torneo.
El partido comenzará a las 21:00 horas, en el estadio Alberto J. Armando, y contará con el arbitraje de Luis Lobo Medina . La transmisión en vivo para todo el país estará a cargo de ESPN Premium. El ganador de la serie avanzará a los cuartos de final, donde se enfrentará a Gimnasia de La Plata .
Luego de consagrarse campeón de la Copa Sudamericana en Colombia, Boca vuelve a la Bombonera, pero no solo para festejar el título . Si bien en el Templo habrá fiesta tras la obtención del primer título internacional del club en 18 años, el equipo del Vasco Arruabarrena volverá a afrontar un partido importantísimo: será ante Independiente Rivadavia, por los octavos de final del Torneo Clausura.
El Xeneize, que también ganó la Tabla Anual, buscará seguir avanzando rumbo a una nueva final (también enfrentará a Platense en la definición de la Copa Argentina). Por su parte, la Lepra mendocina tratará de dar el gran golpe para meterse entre los ocho mejores del certamen. Conocé todos los detalles del partido por acá, en Olé.

title: El tremendo elogio de Jorge Valdano a Jude Bellingham tras la goleada del Real Madrid en la Champions League
description: El volante inglés fue determinante en la remontada frente al PSV. También recibió un reconocimiento especial de su entrenador, José Mourinho.
article_context:
Jude Bellingham en el partido del Real Madrid vs. PSV. (AP)
Con Jude Bellingham como uno de sus grandes protagonistas, el Real Madrid volvió a demostrar su poderío en la Champions League . Los dirigidos por José Mourinho consiguieron una nueva victoria en el certamen continental y la actuación del mediocampista inglés despertó la admiración de Jorge Valdano .
El Merengue goleó 5-1 al PSV en el Santiago Bernabéu, por la quinta fecha de la Fase de Liga. Sin embargo, el desarrollo del encuentro no fue tan sencillo como refleja el resultado final: los españoles debieron revertir la desventaja inicial para quedarse con los tres puntos .
Debido a unas molestias físicas, Bellingham comenzó entre los suplentes e ingresó en el entretiempo, cuando su equipo estaba un tanto abajo en el marcador. La decisión del entrenador portugués dio resultado y el rendimiento del británico no pasó inadvertido para el campeón del mundo con Argentina en México 1986.
Tras la victoria, el exdelantero analizó la actuación del mediocampista en Movistar Plus y aseguró: “ Bellingham está en un momento glorioso, posiblemente no haya en Europa un jugador mediocampista de esa categoría ”.
"No hay un mediocampista en Europa como Bellingham". Jorge Valdano y el liderazgo del 5⃣ del Real Madrid. #UCL #LaCasaDelFútbol pic.twitter.com/rH7SGRjYxA
Más allá de sus condiciones futbolísticas, al argentino le llamó la atención la capacidad de liderazgo del volante a una edad en la que todavía tiene margen para seguir creciendo dentro del fútbol profesional.
“Hay que mirar dos veces la edad que tiene, tiene 23 años, es una cosa increíble lo que le queda todavía de recorrido, porque no ha alcanzado aún la plenitud, ¿no? Se supone que la plenitud llega con 27 años , este chico es joven todavía”, agregó.
Valdano no fue el único que destacó el presente del ex Borussia Dortmund. Durante la conferencia de prensa, el técnico portugués resaltó su influencia en la remontada y ponderó las distintas funciones que puede cumplir dentro de la cancha. “ Es un jugador extraordinario, lo tiene todo: visión, táctica, lo tiene todo y hoy ha cambiado la dirección del partido ”, sostuvo.
Además, aprovechó la oportunidad para cuestionar su ubicación en la última edición del Balón de Oro: “ Para mí es el mejor jugador del centro del campo del mundo , puede jugar de 10, de 8, por eso cuando se habló del Balón de Oro, el escándalo es que no estuviera en el top ten ”.
Así, pese a las molestias físicas que habían condicionado su participación desde el arranque, el inglés volvió a demostrar su importancia en el funcionamiento del conjunto español (metió el 2-1 y asistió en el quinto tanto) y se llevó el reconocimiento tanto de su entrenador como de una figura histórica de la institución .

headline: Valdano elogia a Bellingham tras goleada del Real
caption: Jorge Valdano calificó a Jude Bellingham como el mejor centrocampista de Europa tras la victoria 5‑1 del Real Madrid sobre el PSV en la Champions League. El inglés, que ingresó en el entretiempo pese a molestias físicas, marcó el segundo gol y dio la asistencia del quinto, cambiando la dinámica del partido. Tanto Valdano como José Mourinho subrayaron su visión, táctica y liderazgo a sus 23 años. ¿Podrá Bellingham convertir este reconocimiento en una candidatura al Balón de Oro?

title: La fuerte autocrítica de Erling Haaland por el presente del Manchester City
description: El delantero noruego rompió el silencio tras el empate ante Napoli por la Champions League, en medio de una mala racha deportiva y la incertidumbre institucional.
article_context:
Erling Haaland en el partido de Manchester City vs. Napoli. (EFE)
Erling Haaland atraviesa un momento complicado en el Manchester City . Lo que parecía ser el comienzo de una nueva etapa prometedora bajo la conducción de Enzo Maresca se transformó en un escenario de incertidumbre . Y después de otra jornada lejos de las expectativas en la Champions League, el goleador dejó en evidencia su malestar .
Los Citizens igualaron 2-2 ante Napoli por la quinta fecha de la Fase de Liga. Ayyoub Bouaddi y Rayan Cherki marcaron para los ingleses, mientras que Rasmus Hojlund y Noa Lang convirtieron para el conjunto italiano, que estuvo dos veces arriba en el marcador.
El empate profundizó una mala racha que registra apenas una victoria en los últimos siete compromisos . En ese contexto, el atacante noruego realizó una fuerte autocrítica sobre el funcionamiento colectivo.
“Intentamos presionar, pero no pudimos. No es suficiente. Les permitimos entrar con demasiada facilidad y no pudimos controlar ni atacar el partido como queríamos ”, expresó el delantero en diálogo con TNT Sports.
“El fútbol puede ser tan difícil y tan fácil a la vez. Cuando ganás, todo es fácil y sabés exactamente qué hacer; cuando perdés, empezás a cuestionarlo todo . Lo ideal sería no pensar, pero es difícil en estos momentos”, agregó.
Asimismo, remarcó que “se trata de sacar el máximo provecho de cada jugador” y destacó las herramientas disponibles dentro del plantel: “Tenemos muchísima calidad. Debemos reagruparnos para mantener una actitud positiva y aportar energía al campo ”.
🗣️ "I have no idea what we were missing. You could feel it in the last few games that there's something that's not clicking fully." @Erling reflects on @ManCity 's 2-2 draw with Napoli. 🎤 @AndyKerrtv #UCL | #ManCity pic.twitter.com/Cx2Hzieom3
En declaraciones a beIN Sports, el noruego fue todavía más contundente: “Tenemos que dar más, tenemos que hacerlo mejor. No tengo ni idea de lo que nos ha faltado, pero se está viendo que en los últimos partidos hay algo que no está funcionando ”.
A las dificultades deportivas se suma el proceso judicial por las infracciones al reglamento financiero de la Premier League . En septiembre, una comisión independiente declaró al club culpable de 114 de los 115 cargos . La institución negó haber cometido irregularidades y apeló el fallo.
Por su parte, Maresca, quien días atrás descartó que el conflicto financiero afectara el rendimiento del equipo, fue autocrítico por los 20 tantos recibidos en los últimos diez encuentros : “Estamos recibiendo demasiados goles. Es bastante evidente. Es algo que debemos corregir. Somos capaces de corregirlo ”.
Ahora, los de Manchester visitarán al Arsenal el domingo 29 de noviembre. Sobre ese desafío, Haaland advirtió: “ El próximo partido es contra los campeones . El partido más difícil de la temporada. Necesitamos un rendimiento al máximo nivel ”.

headline: Haaland critica al City tras empate ante Napoli
caption: Erling Haaland rompió el silencio después del 2‑2 de Manchester City contra Napoli en la Champions League, señalando la falta de presión y la dificultad para controlar el juego. El delantero recordó la escasa racha del conjunto, con solo una victoria en los últimos siete partidos, y pidió reagruparse para volver a aprovechar la calidad del plantel. Con la presión financiera del club en el horizonte, la autocrítica llega justo antes del duelo contra el Arsenal. ¿Logrará el City revertir la tendencia antes del próximo compromiso?

title: How to take advantage when LeBron, Embiid or Brown sit
description: Andre Snellings looks at how the 76ers are handling rotations, resting players and dishing out minutes, and explains how to take advantage of it.
article_context:
Through Monday, Nov. 23, the Philadelphia 76ers have played 17 games, and their starting lineup has broken down to four general epochs.
They have had their entire starting five in six games; missed four games each from Joel Embiid and LeBron James and missed three games from Jaylen Brown . Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe have both missed only one game each.
While the stats from handful of games in any given epoch isn't enough to make definitive statements, we can start to see some tendencies. On the fantasy and player prop front, this leads us to revive The 76ers' Player Availability Flowchart.
The players on the team perform differently, based upon which of their teammates are available in a given game.
We know each player's season averages, so let's break down how their production trends and expected values have tended to change based on the absences of their star teammates.
When either Embiid or LeBron have sat, Maxey and the one who played have both increased their scoring volume and scoring efficiency. This tracks, as these are the three best team-offense creators on the team. All three are very comfortable with the ball in their hands, making decisions to generate shots for either themselves or their teammates.
When all are available to play, they each have to play more off the ball than any are used to in their careers. But when one or more of the trio sits, the other(s) get to handle the ball and create their own shot more, which is in their comfort zones. Maxey has only sat out one game this season, but in that game Embiid dropped 26 points and LeBron 22...following a similar trend.
There's still time to join or create a league in the No. 1 fantasy basketball game. Your league starts fresh on the first scoring period following completion of your draft.
In fact, LeBron increased his scoring and efficiency when any of the other starters sat. Including the one game that Edgecombe sat, where LeBron dropped 18 points on 53% from the field. As expected when he joined such a strong lineup, it's clear that LeBron is sacrificing his stats on a per-game basis but can ramp up when called upon.
Interestingly, Brown's and Edgecombe's scoring efficiencies plummet and their volume dips as well when either LeBron or Embiid sit. Unlike LeBron, Brown and Edgecombe are largely iso players and/or finishers. When defenses don't have to focus on LeBron and/or Embiid, the driving lanes and midrange tend to be more clogged and there are fewer dimes coming out of the frontcourt. This has the biggest negative impact on the two starting wings.
On the other hand, when Brown sits, it seems to unleash Edgecombe alongside LeBron while negatively impacting the scoring volume and efficiency of Embiid and Maxey. LeBron and Edgecombe have the most overlapping playing style with Brown, so perhaps his absence lets them play more to their natural tendencies. Meanwhile, Brown is the best wing scorer and off-ball threat on the 76ers, so his absence might allow opponents to focus their defensive energy more on the two primary options in Embiid and Maxey.
The biggest area of applicability for this data is in preparing for back-to-backs. Both Embiid and LeBron are routinely sitting one-half of every back-to-back that the 76ers play, typically not the same one.
Bottom line, the 76ers are a different team when they have their entire starting five available versus when any of them sit. And by recognizing the differences, you can put your fantasy hoops squad, your DFS lineup or your prop bets in better positions to succeed.
headline: LeBron James y Joel Embiid han descansado cuatro partidos cada uno
caption: Los 76ers llevan 17 partidos jugados hasta el 23 de noviembre, con Embiid y LeBron ausentes cuatro partidos cada uno y Brown tres. Cuando alguno de los titulares descansa, Maxey y el suplente que entra elevan su volumen de anotación y eficiencia, mientras Brown y Edgecombe reducen su efectividad.

title: 'Might be better than Kobe': Inside LeBron's first game in Philly -- more than two decades ago
description: Nearly 25 years ago, LeBron won over Philly for the first time -- inside one of the most iconic basketball arenas in the world.
article_context:
Jeremy Treatman, a former high school assistant coach in the Philadelphia suburbs who was running a burgeoning company that staged big-time basketball events between the game's future stars, had just sent a message to Dru Joyce II, the new coach at St. Vincent-St. Mary High School in Akron, Ohio, the school famously led by one of the most highly touted prep prospects in the history of the sport.
Six months after a then-17-year-old LeBron James had appeared on the cover of Sports Illustrated accompanied by the headline, "The Chosen One," Treatman was pitching Joyce on choosing him to build James' hype even more.
How would you like to play at the Palestra in Philly? How would you like to play Madison Square Garden against Sebastian Telfair? How would you like to play at Ohio State? How would you like to play at University of Dayton? How would you like to play in the Dean Dome in North Carolina?
In Philly parlance, Treatman had him at, "Yo."
"He calls me the next day and he says, 'You can get us to play at the Palestra?!'" Treatman told ESPN. "I go, 'Absolutely! Of course.' He goes, 'I've always dreamed of playing in the Palestra. I've heard about this place my whole life.
"I was completely bluffing about the Palestra," Treatman said. "I hadn't talked to anybody."
NAMED BY UNIVERSITY of Pennsylvania professor William N. Bates, evoking the Greek term "palæstra" that describes an athletic competition surrounded by an audience, the Palestra was the home for Penn's basketball, volleyball and wrestling teams.
But its reputation as a hoops haven spread far beyond the corner of S. 33rd St. and Walnut St. on the Quakers' campus.
With its red brick facade, its ceiling suspended by a spine of steel arches and bleachers that practically bleed right onto the maple hardwood playing surface, the Palestra became more than just a gymnasium, earning the nickname "The Cathedral of College Basketball."
It was for decades the home for the famed round-robin Big Five schedule between Philadelphia's college basketball teams and has hosted more NCAA men's basketball games than any other arena in the country.
"Brad Stevens and I, when I worked for him in Boston, we would go back and forth about Hinkle or the Palestra, Hinkle or the Palestra," Detroit Pistons assistant coach Jerome Allen told ESPN.
Allen, a Penn alum, took umbrage with his old boss' preference for Butler University's bandbox.
"[The Palestra] was built in 1926," Allen continued. "The first college game was played in '27. Cameron Indoor Stadium [at Duke University] was modeled after it. And everybody played in it: high school, college. It's a who's who for college basketball."
(The NBA might have sided with Stevens by opting to have the NBA Cup final at Hinkle Fieldhouse this December. But Evan Wasch, the NBA's executive vice president of basketball strategy and growth, recently said the Palestra is "on the list" for consideration to host a future cup championship.)
It was the perfect stage, Treatman thought, to host James, whom he first saw play in person at the Slam Dunk to the Beach tournament in Lewes, Delaware, in December 2001.
"I saw him make an under-the-basket reverse layup that reminded me of Dr. J's move over Mark Landsberger," Treatman said, referring to Julius Erving's iconic bucket for the Philadelphia 76ers in Game 4 of the 1980 NBA Finals against the Los Angeles Lakers .
With the image of a soaring James still fresh in his mind, he dialed Gregg Downer, the head coach at Lower Merion High School, where Treatman used to work as an assistant.
"I called Downer and I said, 'I can't believe what I'm saying, but I think I just saw somebody who might be better than Kobe [Bryant],'" Treatman recalled.
While Joyce prepared his team for James' senior season, Treatman began to make good on his bluff.
He called Peggy Kowalski, the Palestra's box office manager, to get her on board, telling her he was "almost positive" the event would sell out.
Now he just needed an opponent. He wanted to keep it local.
"My idea was not to have them play the best team [in the country], but the best Philly team," Treatman said.
He settled on Strawberry Mansion, a Philadelphia Public League school whose star, 6-foot-2 guard Maureece Rice, was threatening to break the high school scoring record of the man responsible for the most famous 100-point game in history: Wilt Chamberlain .
The game was set: St. Vincent-St. Mary vs. Strawberry Mansion. James vs. Rice. Dec. 22, 2002, at the Palestra.
"To have Bron there," Allen said, "everybody talked about the battle between him and Reece Rice."
FIVE YEARS BEFORE Aron Cohen scored 14 points off the bench to help lift Penn over the Princeton Tigers as a junior guard, he was a high school sophomore sitting in the stands, soaking in the most raucous basketball environment he ever experienced -- before or since.
"I just remember the Palestra being so packed," Cohen told ESPN. "I mean, when I played at Penn, we played against Carolina when they were No. 1 in the country.
"And from what I remember, I felt like that game against LeBron was more packed. ... Just hearing about him, seeing him in SLAM magazine, it was like, 'Wow, this guy is in another world.' You have to see him. You can't miss it if you're a basketball fan."
Former Detroit Pistons guard Richard Hamilton, whose Coatesville, Pennsylvania, high school team lost to Bryant and Lower Merion in the district playoffs at the Palestra in 1996, distinctly remembers the landmark game.
"The Palestra is a big deal for us. That was always the mecca of Philadelphia for us," Hamilton told ESPN. "So when LeBron James comes there ... that was a moment for Philadelphia. Because it was before social media. Nobody got an opportunity to see him. So when you see this man-child coming to the arena with the type of aura that came with it, it was something that my friends and my family talk about to this day."
Treatman delivered on his sellout prognostication -- and then some.
"I had random people coming up to my office on the sixth floor at 1420 Walnut St., knocking on the door: 'You selling tickets? You selling tickets?'" Treatman said. "And I was. I was selling tickets. It was a one-man ticket office. It was hysterical. The phone calls were just nonstop. And the game, they tell me there were more people in the Palestra that night than any time in history."
Among the attendees were current New York Knicks president of basketball operations Leon Rose, a then-influential sports agent w
